userJob: Declare tokens so they exist on every route rather than on some of them
problem: Root custom properties are declared inside a component style block, which is scoped and only ships on routes that render that component, so the direction holds on the home page and reverts on a subpage
worksWhen: Any Astro build with more than one route
avoidWhen: A genuinely component-local value that no other component should read, which is what scoped styles are for
mechanism: Put tokens in one plain stylesheet imported from the base layout. Scoped styles remain the default for everything else, and the global escape hatch is the exception you have a reason for rather than the habit.
risks: Diagnosing the reverted subpage as a CSS specificity problem, when the properties are simply absent
Making everything global to avoid the problem, which loses the scoping the stack gives you for free
mobileRules: A missing token often falls back to an inherited value that happens to look plausible at one width and not another
accessibilityRules: A missing colour token can silently fall back to a value that fails contrast, so measure the subpage rather than the home page

userJob: Structure a set of articles, case notes or entries in Astro
problem: Each entry is written as its own route file, so the set has no schema, no shared template and a hand-maintained file per item
worksWhen: Any repeating editorial content: posts, notes, case entries, catalogue records
avoidWhen: A handful of genuinely singular pages that share nothing, where a collection adds a schema for no benefit
mechanism: Define the schema in the content configuration, keep entries under the content directory, and render them from one dynamic route driven by the static paths function. Run the sync step after touching the schema, or the types and the entries disagree.
risks: A schema loose enough to accept incomplete entries, which pushes the failure into the template
Forgetting the sync after a schema change, which shows as type errors that look unrelated
mobileRules: One template renders every entry, so the longest real entry is the one to check at 375px
accessibilityRules: A single template means one heading structure for the whole set; get it right once rather than per entry
genericnessNote: Content structure is architecture and does not decide how entries look.

userJob: Decide which components ship JavaScript to the browser
problem: A component without a client directive renders once at build and its script never runs, so the control looks correct, does nothing, and reports no error anywhere
worksWhen: Any Astro build with interactive elements
avoidWhen: A fully static page, where there are no islands to record
mechanism: Record every island in the direction record with its directive and its reason. A missing directive produces a control that looks right and is inert. The opposite costs more, because one eager directive on a single button pulls a whole framework runtime onto the page. Two directives on the same component are two roots with separate state, so a header toggle and a drawer built as separate islands disagree about whether the menu is open.
risks: A silent inert control, which no build step reports
Two islands sharing a concept and not sharing state, which produces contradictory interface states
mobileRules: A framework runtime pulled in for one control costs most on a phone
accessibilityRules: An inert control still reads as operable to assistive technology, which is worse than a control that is visibly disabled

userJob: Style content that comes from Markdown or from injected HTML
problem: Scoped selectors never reach markup injected at runtime or rendered from Markdown, because the scoping attribute is added at compile time to elements the compiler can see, so editorial content renders unstyled
worksWhen: Any page rendering Markdown, rich text or injected HTML
avoidWhen: Fully authored components, where scoping works as intended
mechanism: Style injected and Markdown-rendered content from a global rule targeting a container class, rather than from a scoped block. Keep that global rule narrow and named, so it is clear which content it owns.
risks: Making the whole component global to fix one region, which leaks every other rule in it
A global rule broad enough to capture authored components as well, which produces changes nobody traces
mobileRules: Editorial content is where measure and image widths break first at 375px, and it is exactly the content the scoped styles missed
accessibilityRules: Unstyled editorial content usually keeps its semantics, so this reads as a visual bug rather than an accessibility one, but check heading levels the author supplied
genericnessNote: A scoping fact about the compiler.

userJob: Handle values that must be current on a statically built page
problem: A date computed in the frontmatter evaluates at build and freezes into the HTML, so a last-updated line shows the deploy date until someone deploys again
worksWhen: Any statically built Astro page carrying a time, a count or anything that changes
avoidWhen: A value that genuinely is fixed at build, such as a version, where freezing is correct
mechanism: Decide per value whether it is a build-time fact or a request-time fact, and write the choice down. A request-time value needs either an island or a server-rendered route. A build-time value that reads as current is a claim the page cannot support, so either make it current or label it with the date it was taken.
risks: A stale figure presented as live, which is a claim a reader can act on
Adding an island for a value that could simply carry its as-of date
accessibilityRules: An as-of date belongs in text beside the value, not in a title attribute

userJob: Point the verification pass at the output that will actually ship
problem: The matrix runs against the development server while the project has a server adapter configured, so the captured output and the deployed output diverge and the pass proves nothing
avoidWhen: A purely static project with no adapter, where the development server is representative
mechanism: Run against the development server for a static project. If a server adapter is configured, build first and run against the preview server instead, because the two outputs diverge. Run the content sync after touching a collection schema so the types match what will render.
risks: Reporting a pass from an output nobody will deploy
Capturing before the sync, so the run fails on type errors that look like design failures
mobileRules: Adapter output can differ in which assets are inlined, which changes first paint at 375px
accessibilityRules: Server-rendered output can include markup the static build omits, so the accessibility pass has to run against the shipping output
